provenance: Synthetic benchmark authored for this project with a deterministic generator. NOT real university data and NOT independently human-validated. Labels follow the documented classification criteria; review before using them for model selection.
generation: Hand-authored course scenarios expanded deterministically into a complete course-module label matrix. No LLM, external API, or paid service is used.
splitPolicy: 40 development courses (D001-D040) and 60 disjoint test courses (T001-T060). Development data may be used for pipeline sanity checks; test data is reserved for final evaluation. Do not tune labels or thresholds on the test split.
relevanceDefinition: A module is relevant to a course when its ground-truth decision is match or partial. Courses with no match/partial label are excluded from Recall@K, HitRate@K and MRR denominators, matching the existing retrievalMetrics implementation.

straightforward.definition: The course description closely mirrors the target module description and explicit learning outcomes.
straightforward.labelRule: Target module = match; every other module = no_match.

paraphrase.definition: The course covers the same content using synonyms, alternative terminology, or mixed German/English vocabulary.
paraphrase.labelRule: Target module = match; every other module = no_match.

partial.definition: The course covers a proper subset of the target module and explicitly omits important required topics.
partial.labelRule: Target module = partial; every other module = no_match. Partial means content relevance, not partial credit allocation.

hard_negative.definition: The course has one genuine target match but also shares vocabulary with a decoy module that it explicitly does not cover, making lexical overlap misleading.
hard_negative.labelRule: Target module = match; the decoy module and every other module = no_match. Decoy module is recorded in decoyModuleId for analysis only.

no_valid_match.definition: The course belongs to a non-computing or unrelated domain and has no substantive overlap with any target module.

labelingCriteria.match: The documented course content and learning outcomes substantially cover the target module's required topics; relevance is judged on substance, not keyword overlap.
labelingCriteria.partial: A proper subset of the target module is covered and important required topics are explicitly absent. This is retrieval relevance and does not imply partial credit allocation.
labelingCriteria.no_match: The documented content does not substantively cover the module. Hard negatives deliberately share vocabulary while lacking substantive coverage.
labelingCriteria.ambiguityPolicy: Cross-domain courses that share terminology with a module are labeled no_match when the substantive requirements are absent. Decoy modules for hard negatives are recorded in course metadata to make this decision auditable.
